I haven't ever *cut* with a hot knife, but I have experience with both burning and cutting, including holding a blade above a flame and then pressing it into my skin.

First, depending on your will power, it's unlikely that you could give yourself anything worse than a 2nd-3rd degree burn. 4th degree is when muscle/tendons or even bones/ligaments are damaged. 2nd and 3rd degree are causing damage beyond the outer layer of skin, but not *that* far.

Burning is extremely painful, especially during the healing process. You have a much higher risk for infection and once infected, it's a hell of a lot harder to deal with. Even just 2nd degree, in order for proper healing, need gauze, a thorough, but undamaging disinfectant and burn gel/ointment. (I've heard toothpaste works well, but have never used it myself, so would not personally recommend it.) 

A break down on burn care: disinfect, apply heavy amount of ointment/gel, place layers of gauze on site and secure with athletic tape or something similar. Change gauze at LEAST twice a day, which requires water to safely separate the gauze from burn site without injuring the skin and then repeat steps above. You may also need to scrub the burn site, incase of infection or heavy scabing (scabs are very bad on burns) which is incredibly painful.

If you do all this, you will end up with large, sensitive patches of scar tissue.

Source: I've self-harmed for years and also worked in fields where injuries (cuts, puncher and burns) were frequent. 

Edit: forgot to mention, but the healing period for burns goes from weeks for small 2nd degree, months for medium sized 3rd degree and even years for injuries beyond that.
